prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study aimed to assess how well artificial intelligence can create synthetic post-contrast brain MRI images from low-dose inputs to reduce the amount of gadolinium contrast agent used.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The review included twelve studies, the majority of which relied on convolutional neural network architectures.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Across the twelve studies, which involved 3846 patients, the AI-generated images showed a pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.91 dB and a structural similarity index of 91.81%.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Because there was significant variation between the included studies, the combined statistical results were interpreted only as descriptive figures rather than definitive averages.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Qualitative reviews indicated that the synthetic images were generally considered diagnostically acceptable or similar to full-dose images, though subtle differences in how lesions and artifacts appeared were noted.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The authors note that high variation between studies, limited external validation, and a lack of clinically focused diagnostic outcomes restrict the generalizability of the current evidence.
facts.subject: computational
